1. Capacitance Value - The capacitance of the component should be checked. When the capacitance is too high, it may result in overheating. 

2. Voltage Rating - The voltage rating of the capacitor should also be reviewed. It should be sufficiently rated for the voltage in your circuit. 

3. Current - The AC and DC bias conditions should be reviewed. The capacitor’s ESR and ripple current must be within their spec limits. Overheating could result from excessive power dissipation due to ripple current. 

4. Capacitor Materials - The type and quality of dielectric and electrode materials contribute to the performance of the capacitor. 

5. Size and Placement - The size of the capacitor and its placement on the circuit board can correspond to how quickly it can dissipate heat. 

6. Cooling System - The lack of an adequate cooling system may be a reason why a multilayer capacitor is overheating. 

7. Operating Temperature - Ensure the capacitor is within its specified operating temperature range. 

8. Soldering conditions- Too high a temperature or time during the soldering process may damage the component and cause it to overheat.

9. Ambient Temperature- A high ambient temperature may contribute to the overheating of the capacitor.

10. Load Factor- Excessive or improper loading can also cause a capacitor to overheat.  

Always consult with a knowledgeable professional or the manufacturer's specifications when replacing a capacitor to ensure compatibility with your system.
